long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Englewood, New Jersey, Malcolm studied politics and economics at Princeton and briefly owned two Ohio weekly newspapers before serving in the US Army during the Second World War. He then joined the company founded by his father, improved its editorial operation and developed successful products, including an investment newsletter and company-industry report cards.

As publisher and editor-in-chief, Malcolm took full control after his brother Bruce died. Under his leadership, circulation and the family fortune grew as the magazine became internationally identified with entrepreneurial capitalism. He reinforced that identity through a conspicuous but strategic public persona built around art collecting, motorcycling, ballooning and hospitality, remaining chairman and editor-in-chief until his death.
